verdict.rationale: Browserbase markets a fetch capability that converts any URL into markdown or JSON for agent context, which gives LLM-ready output without parsing raw HTML. It runs on real browser sessions that claim to handle CAPTCHAs and login walls, which covers the rendering and blocking concerns. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on the fetch/markdown endpoint (output cleanliness, boilerplate stripping, limits), evidence that blocking handling applies specifically to the fetch path, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can get clean LLM-ready text directly instead of dealing with blocking, rendering, and messy HTML myself

citations.quote: Quickly fetch web context for your agent by converting any URL into HTML, JSON or markdown
When your workflow requires a form, a CAPTCHA, or a login prompt, it's handled.
Your agent logs in, navigates, and pulls data from any website, login walls included.
